marks.gloss_en: התם מתניתין, הכא ברייתא! -- the etrog dispute is in a mishna, this one only in a baraita; the lesser-known cannot be the model for the better-known. Not defended: the stam restates the dictum (אלא...)
the baraita, of Shabbat: three sharpened stones may be brought into the privy
מתקיף לה מר זוטרא: ליסתכן? -- shall he endanger himself?
כלאחר יד -- [he rubs] in a backhanded manner (= p_kilachar_yad)
Rav Yehuda: but not the payis
מיתיבי: ... והמקנח בצרור שקינח בו חבירו -- wiping with a pebble another has wiped with brings on hemorrhoids
לא קשיא: הא בלח, הא ביבש -- this when it is moist, this when it is dry
ואיבעית אימא: כאן מצד אחד, וכאן משני צדדין -- here from one side, here from two sides
ואיבעית אימא: הא דידיה, הא דחבריה -- this is his own, this is his fellow's

ten things bring a person to hemorrhoids: eating reed leaves, vine leaves, vine tendrils, an animal's palate without salt, a fish's spine, salted fish not fully cooked; drinking wine lees; wiping with lime or clay; and wiping with a pebble his fellow wiped with
Rav Yosef: [a stone rained on and blurred] -- if its trace is recognisable, it is permitted
שכל המחובר לקרקע הרי הוא כקרקע -- the baraita's own ground for the purity of those of a gal fixed to the door
למימרא דשיעורא דרבי יהודה נפיש? הא קיימא לן דשיעורא דרבנן נפיש! -- is that to say R' Yehuda's measure is the greater? but we hold the Rabbis' measure is the greater
אמר עולא: חפי פותחת -- the teeth of a key (= p_chaf_chafei_potachat; that this makes R' Yehuda's measure the smaller is the answer's force, not stated in the text)
is that to say that R' Yehuda's measure [for bone] is greater?
bone: enough to make a spoon
a tanna taught: glass -- enough to cut with it two threads at once
a pebble or a stone: [the carrying-out measure is] enough to throw at a bird
וכי טורטני יכניס? -- and will he bring scales into the privy? A measure by olive, nut and egg cannot be applied there; left unanswered, and the Sages vote a handful instead
[Zunin: the stones of the privy, how much is their measure?] They said: an olive's bulk, a nut's bulk and an egg's bulk
